title: Release-signing script re-signs the committed boot record on every completed run, so a stale epoch cannot survive
component: release signing and boot-root enrollment tooling
claim: A candidate suspected that the release-signing script could keep an old-epoch boot-root record when only a version counter changed and the loader root stayed the same, which the kernel would later refuse as stale.
location: tools for release signing (boot-root enrollment and record re-signing steps), kernel's boot-measurement record check
why_not_a_finding: The precondition the candidate needed, an unchanged loader root across a release, cannot hold in the signing script as written. Every signing run re-enrolls the loader's boot root unconditionally, before re-signing the record, and that enrollment draws a fresh random seed on every invocation, so the loader root is new (with overwhelming probability) on every completed run. The record and the version counter it carries always agree once a run completes.
routes_tried: Traced the signing script's own step order: the loader-root enrollment step always runs before the record re-signing step, with no conditional skip.
Traced the enrollment command itself: it draws a fresh random seed from the operating system's own randomness source on every call and writes a new root built from that seed.
Checked whether any other path in the tooling could write the boot-root file without going through this enrollment step: none was found.

steps: Confirmed by reading the signing script's control flow and the enrollment tool's own self-test, which asserts that two different seeds produce two different roots.
The signing process itself was not run end to end, since it requires release signing keys not available to this review.

The core mechanism was re-derived directly from the signing script and the enrollment tool source in an independent clone of the repository: pad_seed is drawn from the operating system randomness source on every enrollment call, and the loader-root enrollment step runs unconditionally before the record re-signing step in the script.
